name: LT1711CMS8#TRPBF
title: LT1711/LT1712 single/dual 4.5 ns rail-to-rail comparators for 3 V, 5 V and ±5 V supplies
summary: The LT1711 (single) and LT1712 (dual) are very fast comparators, 4.5 ns at 20 mV overdrive, with inputs that reach 100 mV beyond both rails and matched complementary rail-to-rail outputs that drive TTL or CMOS. Each comparator has an output latch with a hysteretic control pin. They run from 2.4 V to 12 V single or ±2.4 V to ±6 V split supplies and are specified at 2.7 V, 5 V and ±5 V. The LT1711 comes in 8-lead MSOP, the LT1712 in 16-lead narrow SSOP.

circuits.title: 4× NTSC subcarrier voltage-tunable crystal oscillator
circuits.description: The LT1711 is wired as a 14.31818 MHz crystal oscillator. From the + input, which 2k and 390 Ω bias from 5 V, the feedback runs through 100 pF, the crystal and 15 pF in series, then 100 pF to the Q output; the MV-209 varactor spans the crystal and 15 pF pair, with 1M from its anode to ground. 2k from Q and 200 pF to ground drive the − input. The 0 V to 5 V tuning input passes through the 3.9k/1k divider, the LT1004-2.5 reference, the 1N4148 and the 1M chain to bias the varactor, giving a broad tuning range that is close to symmetric about the centre frequency. The 0.047 µF C SELECT capacitor sets the tuning bandwidth and is picked to suit the phase-lock loop. The inverting output is the frequency output.

parts.note: C SELECT: chosen for the PLL loop response

notes: V+ goes to the 5 V rail; V−, GND and LATCH ENABLE go to ground.
Tuning deviation from the 14.31818 MHz centre exceeds ±240 ppm for a 0 V to 5 V input.

circuits.title: Hysteresis from the inverting output to the inverting input
circuits.description: The input signal goes straight to the + input. The Q̄ output feeds the − input through 50k against 50 Ω to ground, so the − input steps by a small fraction of the output swing each time the comparator switches.
notes: Supplies are V+ = 5V and V− = −5V, and the hysteresis is 5 mV. GND and LATCH ENABLE go to ground.

circuits.title: Hysteresis from the non-inverting output to the non-inverting input
circuits.description: The input arrives through 50 Ω at the + input and the threshold VREF sits on the − input. A 50k from Q back to the + input adds positive feedback.
notes: Supplies are V+ = 5V and V− = −5V, and the hysteresis is 5 mV. GND and LATCH ENABLE go to ground.

circuits.title: Hysteresis on a differential input
circuits.description: A differential signal enters through a 50 Ω resistor into each input. Each output returns to the input of the same sense through 100k: Q to the + input and Q̄ to the − input, giving symmetric positive feedback.
notes: Supplies are V+ = 5V and V− = −5V, and the hysteresis is 5 mV. GND and LATCH ENABLE go to ground.

circuits.title: Simultaneous full-duplex 75 Mbaud interface on two wires
circuits.description: Each end has one LT1712: comparator B drives the line and comparator A receives. The driver's complementary outputs reach the twisted pair through R1 and RO, and the resistive network's input resistance is made equal to the cable's 120 Ω. Each receiver input taps an R2-R3 divider running from a local driver output to the opposite line wire; its ratio lets the receiver reject the large local transmit signal and sense the attenuated signal from the far end. 750k resistors join each receiver output to its input of the same sense, 100k resistors do the same on each driver, and BAV99 diodes connect each line wire to the 3 V rail and to ground. Both ends run from a single 3 V supply.

circuits.title: 1 MHz series-resonant crystal oscillator with square and sine outputs
circuits.description: The crystal's impedance is lowest at its series resonance, so the positive-feedback path through it and R4, from the LT1711 output to its + input (biased by R1 and R2 from VS), sets the circuit oscillating at that frequency. The R3-C1 path to the − input stops the circuit from finding a stable DC operating point. The comparator output is a 1 MHz square wave. The + input carries a sine wave with small glitches where the fast output edges couple back through the crystal capacitance; it passes through R10, C5, R5 and R6 to the LT1806, wired as a bandpass filter with Q = 5 and unity gain at 1 MHz, with its + input set by R9, R8 and C2, and its output is the clean sine.
notes: LT1711 pin numbers: 1 V+, 2 +IN, 3 −IN, 4 V−, 5 LATCH ENABLE, 6 GND, 7 Q, 8 Q̄ (open). LT1806 pins: 2 −IN, 3 +IN, 4 V−, 6 OUT, 7 V+, 1 open.
Square-wave jitter is better than 28 psRMS at VS = 5 V and 40 psRMS at VS = 3 V.
Sine-output distortion: −70 dBc at the second harmonic and −60 dBc at the third.
Sine amplitude follows the comparator's output swing, and so the supply; no amplitude-control loop is needed because the sine is a filtered copy of the square wave.

operation.text: The inputs work from 100 mV below V− to 100 mV above V+ whatever the supply: −5.1 V to 5.1 V on ±5 V, −0.1 V to 5.1 V on a single 5 V. The limit is where the output still answers a small differential input correctly. Inputs driven further beyond the rails do not reverse the output phase. Past the range a substrate PN diode would conduct; Schottky clamps from each input to the supplies keep it off and speed recovery from heavy overdrive. The two inputs may be taken to opposite rails without a large rise in input current.

IB is measured on a 5 V supply with both outputs held at 2.5 V. The input stage pairs an NPN and a PNP differential pair. Close to V− only the PNP pair runs and current leaves the inputs; close to V+ only the NPN pair runs and the current reverses, flowing in; in between it is a mix of both. A large differential input raises the current of one input and lowers the other, so source resistance should be kept low.
The complementary rail-to-rail outputs Q and Q̄ are matched and drive TTL or CMOS logic directly. Each sinks 10 mA to within 0.5 V of GND and sources 10 mA to within 0.7 V of V+.

Each comparator has its own latch: with its LATCH ENABLE pin high the outputs keep their last state, with it low the outputs follow the inputs. Left open the pin drifts low, but for flow-through use it should be tied to ground. The pin accepts TTL or CMOS drive and has about 100 mV of hysteresis, so slow or noisy latch signals do not upset it. On the LT1712, latching the idle comparator when only one is in use avoids interaction between the two.

At these speeds the supply impedance must stay low or the supplies move with the supply current and the part misbehaves or oscillates, and parts sharing an unbypassed rail can interact. Bypass capacitors go as close to the supply pins as possible: a high-frequency 1000 pF ceramic in parallel with larger parts such as 0.1 µF ceramic and 4.7 µF tantalum. Solder their ground ends to the plane that serves the outputs so their currents do not cross the ground under the input circuit, and join the two ground planes only at the board's ground connection (star grounding).

Keep traces short and do not run an output trace beside an input trace. Output traces longer than a few inches need termination, typically 100 Ω to 400 Ω, against reflections. Source impedances should be well below 1 kΩ. Inputs and outputs should be kept apart; on the LT1712, V+, V− and GND traces routed between them shield the inputs from the outputs, with X7R 0805 bypass capacitors beside the GN16 package. Its paired V− pins connect internally yet should also be tied together on the board so that both serve as shields; likewise its paired V+ pins. Its GND pins have no internal connection, and usually both go straight to the ground plane.

Positive feedback from an output to an input suppresses oscillation, at the cost of input sensitivity, so its amount should suit the system. With rail-to-rail inputs and complementary outputs, a feedback resistor can run from either output to the input of the same sense without concern for common-mode range. Three arrangements each give 5 mV of hysteresis on ±5 V supplies: Q̄ through 50k to the − input with 50 Ω to ground; Q through 50k to the + input fed by 50 Ω; and on a differential input, Q to + and Q̄ to − each through 100k, with 50 Ω in each input.

One LT1712 at each end of a twisted pair carries data both ways at once up to 75 Mbaud. Run one way, the eye is wide open; run both ways at once, crosstalk shows as noise and the eye closes slightly but stays good. Because the input range reaches 100 mV past both rails, the link tolerates ±3 V of ground difference between the ends. Other resistor sets work too: start from the cable ZO, choose R1, RO and R2 + R3 so the network's input resistance equals ZO, then split R2 and R3 so the divider ratio is half the attenuation factor.

The voltage-tunable crystal oscillator circuit is a VCXO for a 4× NTSC subcarrier, meant for phase locking. A 0 V to 5 V tuning input gives a broad, fairly symmetric range about 14.31818 MHz: 14.3140 MHz at 0 V to 14.3217 MHz at 5 V, more than ±240 ppm. The C SELECT capacitor sets the tuning bandwidth and is chosen to suit the loop response.

In the 1 MHz oscillator the comparator output is the square wave; the signal on its + input across the crystal is a sine with small glitches from the output edges coupling through the crystal capacitance. The LT1806 bandpass stage, Q = 5 at 1 MHz, removes the glitches and buffers the sine.
